subject: Chemistry
solution:
A: $\mathrm{H_2,\ Pd{-}BaSO_4}$ partially reduces an acid chloride to an aldehyde: $\mathrm{RCOCl + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd-BaSO_4} RCHO + HCl}$. This is the Rosenmund reduction, so A → II.
B: $\mathrm{SnCl_2,\ HCl}$ reduces a nitrile to an imine, and hydrolysis of the imine gives an aldehyde: $\mathrm{RCN \to RCH{=}NH \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} RCHO}$. This is the Stephen reaction, so B → IV.
C: Chromyl chloride, $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ in $\mathrm{CS_2}$, oxidises toluene to a chromium complex, and hydrolysis of the complex gives benzaldehyde. This is the Etard reaction, so C → I.
D: $\mathrm{CO,\ HCl}$ with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (or CuCl) converts benzene into benzaldehyde. This is the Gattermann–Koch reaction, so D → III.
So the matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Answer: (D)
